openings.claim: Refine the existing coloured material-type tray tags with pencilled pattern-specific quantities. At pickup, each volunteer uses the tag to identify the material and its required quantity. This extends parent A's own tray-cue function; its benefit remains untested.
openings.delta: Keep the existing trays and colour identities; add quantity cues to their existing tags. Include annotation time within the assembly budget. This proposal does not establish solutions to replenishment, crossing reaches, envelope identification or omissions during filling.
openings.prediction: If shared-material omissions originate in quantity selection, tagged quantities should reduce wrong picks and subsequent omissions. Success for participants and assemblers still requires all 60 assigned-pattern kits within 90 minutes, with at most one correction at distribution.
openings.rival_prediction: The nearest alternative is that volunteers pick correct quantities but lose items while filling envelopes. Under that explanation, tag quantity cues leave filling-stage omissions largely unchanged. O4 also permits an access-related explanation, though its pattern mixture is unknown.
openings.defeat: Correct recorded picks followed by repeated filling omissions would defeat the proposed causal explanation. More than one distribution correction or failure to complete all 60 kits within 90 minutes would defeat its sufficiency for this task.
openings.probe: Propose a 60-kit run using exactly two volunteers, existing envelopes, pencils, trays and tally sheets on the existing table. Count annotation, assembly and checking within 90 minutes. Record pickup discrepancies separately from envelope omissions; audit specified quantities and dimensions and record assigned-pattern corrections at distribution. Stop at the time limit; incomplete kits count as failure.
assumptions: Existing tags have enough writable, legible space for the quantities; this capability is unconfirmed.
The authoritative quantities and dimensions for each assigned pattern are available to transcribe accurately; their actual values were not supplied.
Annotation, recording and checking can fit within the unchanged two-volunteer, 90-minute budget; this is unproven.
Conditional fit concerns unverified feasibility, not permission to relax any hard constraint. The proposed probe and eventual intervention have no verified benefit.
